Definition: from G1223 and G1209; to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to:--come after.
BiblicalUsage: To receive in turn is to come after another in the same place. Stephen says the fathers received the tabernacle and brought it in with Joshua, taking up the work the generation before them had carried.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the faith is handed down, not invented; one generation receives what the last one carried, and the tabernacle came into the land because faithful men took their turn.
